title: Component health scoring and lightweight RFC triage for contributions
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: Our contributor guidance and deprecation signals are currently scattered across docs and informal Slack threads. This ticket proposes a formal, lightweight RFC triage process plus a numeric "component health score" to drive maintenance prioritization, deprecation decisions, and contributor feedback loops. The goal is to reduce surprise removals, make upgrade paths clearer, and create objective signals that product and engineering can act on.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented health scoring rubric published in the Design Handbook and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md. 2) A 3-tier RFC triage flow (Fast Path, Standard, and Major) with clear entry criteria and reviewer roles. 3) A deprecation signal matrix tied to health score thresholds and migration support steps. 4) Prototype dashboard mock in Figma and a GH issues template for health reviews.
description_details: Health score dimensions (proposed): usage (monthly references in codebase/docs), visual-regression test coverage, automated accessibility pass rate, number of open incidents/bugs in last 90d, maintenance burden (owner count and PR velocity), dependency risk (legacy tokens/tech), and cross-team ownership. Scores normalized 0-100. Suggested thresholds: >=75: healthy; 50-74: monitor (flag in roadmap); <50: candidate for focused work or deprecation planning. RFC triage: Fast Path (visual tweaks, token naming fixes) -> single reviewer, 2-day SLA; Standard (new component, behavior changes) -> design + eng review, 5-day SLA; Major (breaking API, deprecation) -> cross-functional RFC, impact assessment, 2-week review cycle.
implementation_notes: Trade-offs considered: keeping scoring lightweight vs. exhaustive metrics. We intentionally prefer a small set of signals to avoid heavy instrumentation. We'll start with datasetable metrics from GitHub (references), Storybook usage metrics, and a simple accessibility lint pass. Long-term: integrate with console metrics (runtime usage) via ENG tickets. We will not auto-deprecate; scoring is advisory and requires human sign-off from component steward.
